details.label: Summary
details.text: The threat for at least isolated severe weather is expected to increase by early to mid afternoon. Convective trends are being monitored for a possible severe thunderstorm watch

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Mid-morning mesoanalysis indicates a weak surface low between Sumter and Florence, SC along a quasi-stationary surface boundary extending along the Carolina coastal plain. Ahead of the front, the 12Z Charleston, SC and Newport, NC soundings sampled a very moist boundary layer with dewpoints in the mid to upper 70s, which yielded a strongly unstable environment with MLCAPE of 3000-4000 J/kg. Visible satellite imagery indicates deepening cumulus along the developing sea breeze near the SC-NC border, which will likely evolve into thunderstorms over the next couple of hours with continued heating and destabilization of the boundary layer. Additional storms are possible farther inland ahead of the surface low and along the synoptic front. However, latest CAM guidance suggests the greatest storm coverage along the sea breeze and trailing outflow boundary from storms moving toward the NC Outer Banks. The region resides within the southern fringe of stronger mid/upper-level winds attendant to troughing over the Northeast with around 30 kt of deep-layer shear present across the narrow warm sector. As such, the potential exists for some storm organization, including periodic supercell structures with an associated risk for damaging wind gusts and perhaps marginally severe hail. A brief tornado risk may also materialize given a supercell storm mode along the existing boundaries. The potentially limited geographic extent of the threat area leads to uncertainty in a severe thunderstorm watch issuance

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Recent trends in volumetric radar and IR satellite data indicate at least a temporary deepening of convective updrafts from west through north of Yazoo City, along the leading edge of an elongated MCS that extends into central AR. The 12Z Jackson, MS and Slidell, LA soundings sampled the presence of a very moist inflow air mass, characterized by boundary-layer dewpoints in the mid to upper 70s, yielding MUCAPE of 3000-4000 J/kg. That instability will fuel a gradual increase in storm coverage and intensity through the remainder of the morning along and slightly ahead of the system cold pool as temperatures warm and low-level lapse rates steepen. The instability in conjunction with some enhancement of northwest winds above 3 km AGL per the current Little Rock, AR and Memphis, TN VWPs will support the development of a potentially intense cold pool with some explicit CAM wind gust data indicating wind gusts up to 60-65 mph
